questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to hold your breath underwater for longer
The history of Olympic swimming races
Why swimming is so good for your health
Artistic swimming and one top swimmer's life
questions.why: They discuss how demanding artistic swimming is and hear from swimmer Silvia Solymosyová.

questions.q: What does Phil say about his own physical challenges?
options: He has run several marathons in big cities
He has climbed mountains, but only small ones
He used to be an artistic swimmer at school
He has never done any sport in his life
questions.why: Phil says he's climbed some mountains, 'but only very little ones'.

questions.q: Why did Silvia Solymosyová become famous on social media?
options: Videos of her walking upside down underwater
Because she won an Olympic gold medal
Because she teaches swimming lessons online
Because of her popular dance videos on land
questions.why: She has over a million followers after videos of her walking upside down underwater went viral.

questions.q: How many people can take part in a team routine, according to Silvia?
options: Two
Four
Eight or ten
Up to twenty
questions.why: She says team routines can have eight or ten people.

questions.q: Why do artistic swimmers smile during their routines, according to Silvia?
options: To hide how hard it is, as people think it's easy
Because they are really enjoying themselves
Because the judges ask them to smile
Because smiling helps them breathe underwater
questions.why: She says they smile but are 'hiding behind the smile' with no oxygen; people think it's easy.

options: Two hours every day
Four hours, three days a week
Only at weekends
Eight hours a day, six days a week
questions.why: Phil says Silvia trains eight hours a day, six days a week.

questions.q: What does Silvia think about being coached by her mum?
options: It's only good, because her mum is a champion
It's good and bad: more practice, less rest
It's only bad, and she wants a new coach soon
It makes no real difference to her at all
questions.why: She says it's good because you practise more at home, but on the other hand you train when you should be chillin'.

questions.q: What does Phil suggest when he says he needs 'a respite' from the talk about training?
options: He wants to start artistic swimming himself
He is bored of hearing about artistic swimming
He jokes that even hearing about it is tiring
He thinks Silvia trains far too little
questions.why: After hearing about Silvia's non-stop training, he jokes that he needs a break from the talk.
